data.title: Traffic woes prompt calls for upgrades
data.description: Transport Minister Phiphat Ratchakitprakarn has ordered agencies to assess measures to ease Phuket’s traffic congestion and improve road safety following a meeting with local business leaders.

data.title: Smaller contractors say rooftop solar terms too strict
data.description: Smaller contractors risk being shut out of the government’s 50-billion-baht solar rooftop programme because of stringent requirements that could discourage them from participating, according to an industry group.

data.title: Luxury villa operator faces charges
data.description: PHUKET: Immigration police have arrested a Chinese woman accused of using Thai nominees to operate a luxury villa rental business worth more than 50 million baht.

data.title: High hopes Udon Thani horticulture expo will justify cost
data.description: UDON THANI - The International Horticultural Expo 2026, a 2.5-billion-baht investment, has been readied for public viewing with hopes it will stimulate the local economy and justify its considerable cost.

data.title: Jewish leader’s relatives, 19 firms under scrutiny after citizenship revoked
data.description: The Interior Ministry and the Department of Special Investigation (DSI) are examining the descendants of Jewish community leader Yosef Chaim Kantor and 19 companies linked to him after his Thai citizenship was revoked.

data.title: Charity boss suspended
data.description: The Good Deeds Foundation has temporarily suspended its president, actress Panadda “Bum” Wongphudee, and halted donations pending an investigation into financial transactions linked to the construction of its facilities in Pathum Thani.

data.title: Thailand ready to evacuate citizens if Mideast tensions escalate
data.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow has reaffirmed Thailand’s readiness to respond to developments in the Middle East, saying preparations are under way to evacuate Thai nationals if necessary, amid reports that the United States may launch another military operation against Iran.

data.title: Land sought for fossil museum in Phetchabun
data.description: PHETCHABUN: Ban Phot Municipality is seeking permission to use 23 rai of agricultural reform land to develop an open-air museum at a fossil site located in Nong Phai district of this northern province.

data.title: iLaw chief seeks dismissal of PM defamation case
data.description: Yingcheep Atchanont, director of the Internet Law Reform Dialogue (iLaw), has urged the Criminal Court to dismiss a defamation case brought against him by Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul.

data.title: PM files ‘tea money’ defamation complaints
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has filed police complaints against opposition MP Rukchanok “Ice” Srinork and the owner of the “Godd Dam” Facebook page over the circulation of a fake claim linking him to a 7-million-baht “tea money” payment.

data.title: Thai-Singaporean sex procurement ring busted
data.description: Police have arrested five people — two Singaporeans and three Thais — accused of recruiting Thai women for prostitution in Singapore and advertising their services online.

data.title: Suvarnabhumi runway subsidence probed after plane gets stuck
data.description: The Ministry of Transport is investigating runway subsidence at Thailand’s biggest airport, Suvarnabhumi, after the landing gear of a China Airlines plane got stuck in the runway surface.

data.title: Bangkok Post secures website following brief disruption
data.description: The Bangkok Post website experienced a brief technical disruption on Thursday morning after unauthorised content appeared on its homepage and other pages.

data.title: ‘Sin tax’ revenue shake-up draws fire
data.description: Four proposed legal amendments could put about 14 billion baht a year in funding for health promotion, public broadcasting, elderly welfare and sports development at the government's discretion, prompting public opposition to plans to end their automatic share of alcohol and tobacco tax revenue.

data.title: PM denies solar project favours big firms
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on Wednesday criticised media reports linking major corporations, including Sino-Thai Engineering and Construction Plc, to the government's household solar rooftop scheme, rejecting claims that the project was designed to favour large businesses.

data.title: Myanmar workers wanted for employer’s killing surrender
data.description: Two married couples from Myanmar, wanted in connection with the killing of their Chinese employer in Bangkok, have surrendered to police after hiding in sugarcane fields in Phanat Nikhom district of Chon Buri.

data.title: Nurses oppose community volunteer plan
data.description: The Nurses Association of Thailand has opposed the government's Community Nursing Volunteer initiative, urging authorities to review the policy and promote oversight to protect patient safety and healthcare standards.

data.title: No need for stockpiling, Ministry of Defence clarifies
data.description: Thailand’s Ministry of Defence issued a statement on Thursday clarifying that the public does not need to stockpile food, water or medical supplies in response to escalating tensions in the Middle East.

data.title: Nurses oppose govt volunteer plans
data.description: The Nurses Association of Thailand has opposed the government's Community Nursing Volunteer initiative, urging authorities to review the policy and promote oversight to protect patient safety and healthcare standards.

data.title: hello bangkokpost, you've been compromised
data.description: The government is preparing to accept a grant worth over 115 million baht from the World Bank to support preparations for a 165-billion-baht flood diversion canal project aimed at reducing flood risks in the lower Chao Phraya basin.
